method: No audio playback was possible. Momentary loudness (EBU R128, 100 ms) was measured on mix/master.wav and narration/narration.wav and set against absolute line times from narration/timeline.json. Music-to-voice was estimated per line as master minus (narration + 2.46 dB master gain). Also checked: per-line wpm, clip head/tail peaks, chunk grouping in lines.json, cue joins against line times, all 21 cue notes and spectrograms (m01, m10, m11, m13, m21 inspected), voice.json and lexicon.json, STT round-trips, and the contact sheets for ch01-s01, ch03-s08 and ch15-s10.
summary: The technical targets are met: -16.0 LUFS, -2.2 dBTP, LRA 6.5. Music sits a median 12.5 dB under the voice, and narration line levels have a p5-p95 spread of 3.2 dB. The score design is ambitious and coherent: a held-note candle leitmotif, a tonal plan, scored silences, and an unresolved Asus4 ending. Seven things keep the sound below excellent. (1) The prologue is the fastest-spoken part of the film: 181 wpm, with L0101 at 264 wpm. The brief asks for an unhurried voice. (2) Ten lines carry fragments of the neighbouring line at chunk-split edges, heard as clicks or ghost syllables. (3) About eight lines have music within 4-6 dB of the voice. Three of them matter most: the Florence swell running into 'Fair credit', the worked numbers in the attention example, and the film's thesis line 'The board was a network all along'. (4) Explicit `spoken` fields bypass the lexicon, so Uszkoreit, Amodei, Hochreiter/Schmidhuber and Rumelhart go out unrespelled and unverified. (5) 17 of 20 cue crossfades fall under a chapter's first line, which buries each new chapter's musical arrival. (6) There are several holes of digital silence, the longest a 17 s stretch over the end cards. (7) Some QA checks are vacuous, so they report a pass without measuring anything.

issues.problem: The prologue is the most rushed passage in the film: ch01 runs at 181 wpm against a film median of 154 and the voice's locked 143.5. L0101 'Here is a small wonder.' runs 264 wpm (1.14 s), L0102 229, L0103 217, L0109 'Put that in the case file.' 248, and L0114 249. The first 60 seconds set the narrator's character, and the brief asks for 'slow, distinguished, unhurried'.
issues.fix: Re-narrate L0101, L0102, L0103, L0109 and L0114 as single-line generations at speed 0.85-0.88, with commas or a dash in `spoken` where a breath belongs ('Here is... a small wonder.'). Target 140-160 wpm. Then re-fit ch01 shot timing and m01's hits.

issues.problem: Several short reveal or cliffhanger lines are clipped quick and lose their weight: L0220 'The paper that put it out had Pitts's own name on it.' at 250 wpm, L0207 'The nets could not learn.' at 235, L0320 (chapter-3 cliffhanger) at 232, L0612 'Who paid for dinner?' at 265, and L0505b at 223.
issues.fix: Re-narrate these lines singly at speed 0.88, or add a comma or pause in `spoken` before the turn word ('had Pitts's own name... on it'). Keep the existing hold after each.

issues.problem: Chunk-split artifacts. Lines generated together in one chunk and then split leave residue of the adjacent line at the clip edges. Peaks in the first or last 30 ms reach -22 to -28 dBFS where they should be near silence. L0704's tail (-22.3 dBFS) holds the onset of L0705 'A crowd did it', which will play as a ghost syllable or stutter. The same pattern affects the heads of L0105, L0204, L0522, L0810, L1216, L1524 and L1307b, and the tails of L0319 and L0401. Automated QA only warns on this ('clipEdges').
issues.fix: In the narrate split step, cut each chunk at the minimum-energy point between the alignment's last word end and the next word start. Apply 15-30 ms fades on both sides and require edge peaks below -50 dBFS. Re-narrate singly any line that has no clean gap. Re-run clipEdges and make it a fail when an edge exceeds -45 dBFS.

issues.problem: Pronunciation risk: 'Jakob Uszkoreit' sits in an explicit `spoken` field, so the lexicon entry (Oosh-ko-rite) never fires. The name is unrespelled and was not in the STT or listen pass, and English TTS commonly reads it 'Us-ko-reet'. It is a named Transformer author in the film's deep dive.
issues.fix: Put the respelling in L1006's `spoken` ('Jakob Oosh-ko-rite', or an unhyphenated variant if it sounds choppy). Re-narrate, then add the line to the STT targets and a human listen check.

issues.problem: 'Dario and Daniela Amodei' is in an explicit `spoken` field, so the lexicon's 'Ah-mo-day' does not fire and the name is unverified. Mispronouncing the founders' name in the one segment about Anthropic is a credibility risk.
issues.fix: Respell in `spoken` (for example 'Ah-mo-day'), re-narrate L1206, and add it to the STT and listen targets.

issues.problem: 'Hochreiter and Schmidhuber's' (L0614) and 'Rumelhart' (L0507) are unrespelled inside explicit `spoken` fields and were not verified. The lexicon entries for Schmidhuber and Rumelhart exist but never fire.
issues.fix: Audition both names, respelling only if they fail ('Hoke-ryter', 'Shmid-hoober', 'Roomel-hart'). Add both lines to the STT and listen pass.

issues.problem: Process gap: generator/film/lib/text.mjs gives an explicit `spoken` field priority over the lexicon, so every respelling must be maintained by hand in 83 lines. The STT pass covered only the 9 lines where the lexicon fires, leaving the riskiest names unchecked. Spellings are also inconsistent: 'AlphaGo' in L0906 vs 'Alpha Go' in L0905b, and 'DeepSeek' in L1406/L1420 vs 'Deep Seek' in L1408b.
issues.fix: Apply lexicon substitution inside `spoken` text too, skipping tokens already respelled. Extend STT targets to every line containing a proper noun from the cast list.

issues.problem: The Florence 'cliff' swell peaks on top of the next line instead of before it. Music-only momentary loudness climbs from -16.7 at 985.5 to -12.7 LUFS at 989.0, but L0834 'Fair credit: that was seven networks voting' starts at 988.62. At its first word the music is about 4-5 dB louder than the narrator, which masks the caveat that keeps the AlexNet numbers honest. The cue notes ask for the peak 'before the next line at 988.63'.
issues.fix: Peak the swell at about 986.8-987.2 and drop it at least 8 dB by 988.3 (taper the last ostinato bar, or apply a 1-s gain ramp in the stem). Keep the 'Fair credit' bed at intensity 0.3 or below and under D3/above D5 through 993.4.

issues.problem: The network wave builds under the film's thesis line. During L1514 'Never one person. The board was a network all along.' (1924.04-1927.85) the music sits about 4 dB under the voice at median and up to 1.5 dB above it at p90. Master momentary reaches -11.8 LUFS at 1926.5, the loudest point of the ending, while the line is still being spoken. The cue notes promised the build would stay below D3 and above D5 until 'network' and bloom in the gap.
issues.fix: Hold the seven era layers at roughly a third of their velocity, with lpf 900 on anything between D3 and D5, until 1927.85. Move every layer's sustain onset so the full D-major bloom starts at 1927.9 or later, as the notes specify. Target music at least 10 dB under the voice for the whole line.

issues.problem: In the worked attention example, the four 'score' plucks (C#5 A4 E5 C#5, inside the speech band) are placed on the spoken numbers. During L1012 'The scores: two, nothing, four, two. Then we halve them.' the music rises to the voice's level (p90 about -1 dB re voice). The pouring arpeggio under L1013/L1014 is also within 9 dB. The numbers are the content of the deep dive and must be crystal clear. The m12 to m13 crossfade also sits under L1002 at 1134.9, with music within about 6 dB.
issues.fix: Put each score pluck in the micro-gap after its number, not on it, or move them to D6 and above at half velocity. Keep the pour arpeggio above D5 or after 1226.4. Start m13's entrance 2 s earlier, at 1132, so the crossfade finishes before L1002.

issues.problem: Two Shores masks two short, important lines. L1417 'A newer candle: the gap is months, not years.' has music about 4 dB under the voice at median and above it at p90. The gap-candle rising fourth (1752.47) lands on the line, which is itself 3.3 dB quieter than the narration median. L1409 'A week later, markets fell.' sits on top of the 'sudden low swell' (music within about 6 dB). Right after it the music cuts to digital silence (-98 dBFS) for 3.5 s (1699.3-1702.8), which can read as a dropout.
issues.fix: Move the gap-candle fourth to after the line ends (about 1755.7), or lift it to D6 or above. Shorten the low swell so it peaks after 'fell' (about 1698.1). Under the hold, keep a near-silent floor (room tone or a ppp harmonic at about -45 LUFS) instead of true zero.

issues.problem: L1307b 'In March, an open letter asked for a pause. None came.' (1580.9) has music within about 5 dB at median and -0.8 dB at p90. The line is also the quietest in the film (-21.7 LUFS momentary median against a -17.8 narration median), so 'None came' (the beat's payoff) is at risk.
issues.fix: Thin m17 to the cello pedal alone, below D3, from 1580.5 to 1586, with no horn or string entries during the line. Combine with the line gain fix on L1307b.

issues.problem: A few lines came out 3-4 dB quieter than the narration median and sit exactly where music crowds them: L1307b at -21.7, L1417 at -21.1 and L1501 at -21.1, against a median of -17.8. The lineLevels QA check cannot catch this (see the QA-tooling issue).
issues.fix: Apply +3 dB clip gain to L1307b, L1417 and L1501 (and +2 dB to L0312 and L1011), or re-narrate them with stability 0.5 for more projection.

issues.problem: The Mark I motor-whirr bursts (brown noise, broadband) are placed on content words ('wrong', 'turn') in L0308 'When it was wrong, only the knobs of lit wires turned'. Music there is about 6.7 dB under the voice at median and above it at p90, so noise bursts land on consonants. Separately, the cue falls to -74 dBFS for about 2 s (276.7-278.4) at the end of a 15-s music-only hold, which sounds like a dropout rather than a rest.
issues.fix: Place the whirrs in the gaps after 'wrong' and after 'turned', or high-pass them above 2.5 kHz at -6 dB while he speaks. Bridge 276.5-278.1 with the tender organ chord's tail or room tone so the cut to ch03-s08 lands on sound.

issues.problem: The music-only swell between L0810 and L0811 (880.2-883.0, peaking at -13.1 LUFS M) is still at full level when L0811 'Nobody cut these stencils' starts at 883.0. Music is within about 2 dB of the voice on the first words.
issues.fix: Peak the swell at about 881.3 and decay it at least 8 dB by 882.8.

issues.problem: Cue transitions are almost all buried under speech. 17 of 20 crossfades contain the first line of a chapter (L0201, L0301, L0401, L0406, L0501, L0513, L0601, L0701, L0802, L0820, L0901, L1002, L1110, L1212, L1401, L1501, L1522). Each new chapter's change of key and colour, which the motif plan is built around (G for the 1940s, C organ for 1958, D minor for the winter, F for the thaw), therefore arrives under the narrator's first words instead of in the clear.
issues.fix: Move each incoming cue's start (and the outgoing cue's end) 1.5-3 s earlier, so the crossfade completes and the new cue's first gesture sounds in a music-only gap before the chapter's first line. Where the clock has no gap, ask the shot or timeline owner to add a 1.5-2 s head-hold at chapter openers (ch02, ch03, ch05, ch08, ch10, ch14, ch15).

issues.problem: Digital-zero holes. Apart from the scored rests (which are good), the master falls to true silence (-inf or below -70 dBFS) at 276.7-278.4, 1699.3-1702.8 and 1906.5-1908.5, and for the final 17.2 s (1983.5-2000.7) over the credit and sources cards. In a film whose frame story has tape hiss and room tone, true zero reads as a playback fault, and 17 s of dead air at the end invites viewers to close the tab before the sources card.
issues.fix: Add a continuous room-tone/tape-hiss floor at about -55 to -60 LUFS on its own bus (the m01 hiss: pink, hpf 2.5k), present everywhere except a deliberate 0.5-s total-black beat if wanted. For ch15-s10, either keep m21's ring-out tail decaying to about 1990 or add a very soft held D with hiss under the credit card, fading to zero at 2000.

issues.problem: Sub-bass build-up. Every inspected spectrogram (m01, m10, m11, m13) shows energy from 20 to 50 Hz as strong as the 100-200 Hz band (contrabass D1/D2 drones plus loop-swelling bowed samples). This spends master headroom (the limiter takes 0.94 dB) and will boom on large systems while disappearing on phones. It also thickens the 100-250 Hz region where the narrator's fundamental sits.
issues.fix: Put a 35 Hz high-pass (24 dB/oct) on the music bus and a -2 to -3 dB low shelf at 120 Hz, keyed to the narration sidechain. Re-check the duck depth afterwards; it should come up toward the 3 dB target.

issues.problem: Quoted speech is handled inconsistently. Some `spoken` fields keep quotation marks (L0312, L0318, L0512, L1303, L1304) and others strip them (L0108, L0303, L0405, L0609, L0610, L1518 and more). Without quote marks, the TTS reads quotes as the narrator's own assertion. This matters most for the film's last word, L1518 ('The future depends on some graduate student...'), which should sound like a quotation, and for L0610, where Vapnik's 'no one in his right mind' runs straight on from narration.
issues.fix: Restore quotation marks (or a colon plus a short pause) in `spoken` for every verbatim quote. Re-narrate L1518 and L0610 first and listen for the shift into quotation.

issues.problem: Some QA checks are vacuous. 'lineLevels' reports M = -14.79 for every one of the 223 lines (identical values), so it measures the same window each time and cannot catch the 3-4 dB quiet lines above. 'fadeAfterStrike' is unverified for all 20 cues because cues.json has no lastStrike markers. STT covers only lexicon-fired lines. All three currently report passes without real verification.
issues.fix: Fix lineLevels to measure each line's own window (shot start + line start/end). Have film-score write lastStrike per cue from the Strudel event lists. Extend STT targets to every line containing a proper noun.

best_moments: The scored silence after the film's last quote: the master drops to about -75 dBFS from 1958.9 to 1962.0 before 'Somewhere tonight a lamp is on', exactly as designed. That silence is the most confident sound choice in the film.

Florence: two full beats of nothing on the number (981.9-984.2) through 'A cliff.', then M1 re-enters as a swelling D-major ostinato. The idea is right; only the peak needs to arrive a second earlier.
m05, the first winter: the emptiest music in the film (music-only median -31.9 LUFS against -21 to -26 elsewhere). The density literally follows the snow.

The governing leitmotif: a belief is a held note that is lit (rising fourth), doubted (the harmony moves under it into a sus4) and gone (falls a step). It is carried through era-specific orchestration, and the film ends on the unresolved Asus4 ringing into the Turing card, so 'the case is open' is heard as well as said.

Mix hygiene: -16.0 LUFS integrated, -2.2 dBTP, LRA 6.5. Music sits a median 12.5 dB under speech, narration lines have a p5-p95 spread of 3.2 dB, and all 21 cue renders are within -21.3 to -23.9 LUFS, with no Strudel render errors or clipped samples.
